snippets.output: Blepharitis is an inflammatory condition of the eyelids characterized by redness, swelling, and irritation of the eyelid margins.
Blepharitis is a common condition that can be caused by a combination of factors, including bacterial infestation, Demodex mite infestation, meibomian gland dysfunction, and seborrheic dermatitis.
Blepharitis can cause itching, burning, or stinging in the eyes, along with crusting and flaking of the eyelid margins.
There are two main types of blepharitis: anterior blepharitis, which affects the front of the eyelid, and posterior blepharitis, which affects the back of the eyelid.
Anterior blepharitis is often caused by bacterial infestation or Demodex mite infestation, and posterior blepharitis is often associated with meibomian gland dysfunction.
Blepharitis can be treated with warm compresses, lid hygiene, antibiotic medications, and anti-inflammatory medications.
In severe cases of blepharitis, more aggressive treatments may be necessary, including oral antibiotics and corticosteroids.
